summary: A HEADERS block with more than 24,576 unique header fields panics in HeaderMap::append, crashing the connection task on one remote request.
The write path busy-loops at 100% CPU forever when the transport's poll_write returns Ok(0), because zero-byte writes are retried without progress.
Conflicting duplicate content-length headers are accepted; only the first value is used instead of rejecting the message as malformed.
A response with no :status pseudo-header is accepted and surfaced to the client as 200 OK instead of being a stream error.
On GOAWAY, streams above last_stream_id are closed regardless of initiator, so a client's GOAWAY(0) kills the server's in-progress responses on client-initiated streams.
DATA received after local GOAWAY on a stream above max_stream_id is dropped without connection flow-control accounting, leaking the connection window.
